newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT- Coffee seen sliding towards October lows.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Coffee seen sliding towards October lows.

text.p: JAN Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
London robusta coffee futures took a fresh dive below $1,400 on Wednesday and charts are indicating a slide towards the October low of $1,360 basis January.
The pre-opening call on Thursday was unchanged after small losses in New York overnight.
Traders expected dealings to be thin on Thursday and Friday, with New York closed for Thanksgiving.
Technically, however, Wednesday's move below the $1,400 mark was seen as discouraging.
"The close below $1,400 was technically bearish. There is now a bit of room on the downside," said Darren Gurner, analyst at Sucden.
After a November peak of $1,476, January coffee had been ranging with the low around $1,410-15.
"It now looks like the market started a fresh downtrend from $1,476," said Gurner.
The near-term moving averages were beginning to point downwards which also confirmed the downtrend, he said. The 14-day RSI was neutral at 39 percent.
On the news front, Brazil port workers called off a two-day strike and returned to work late on Wednesday after controversial rules were removed from a new shipping bill.
Traders are awaiting a forecast of the Brazilian 1997/98 crop this week or next by former USDA analyst Leon Yallouz. This will be the first independent report on the crop.
